plainEnglish.text: Makes the office of Morgan Hill City Treasurer appointive.

argAgainst.location: Measure A entry, county List of Local Measures page

fiscal.text: Raises the hotel tax rate from 9% to a maximum of 13%, set by Council resolution, providing $700,000 annually, until ended by voters.

fiscal.location: Ballot question, county List of Local Measures page

yes.text: A yes vote raises the Gilroy hotel tax from 9% to 11% at first, and lets the City Council adjust the rate by resolution up to 13%.
yes.excerpt: If approved by voters, Measure B amends the Hotel Tax Ordinance set forth in Chapter 25A.2 of the Gilroy City Code to initially increase the Hotel Tax rate by 2% from the current rate of 9% to 11%. In addition, Measure B amends the Hotel Tax Ordinance to provide that the City Council may by resolution adjust the rate of the Hotel Tax upwards or downwards without a vote of the people provided that the rate does not exceed 13%.

no.text: If you vote no, this change would not be made.
no.excerpt: If approved by voters, Measure B amends the Hotel Tax Ordinance set forth in Chapter 25A.2 of the Gilroy City Code to initially increase the Hotel Tax rate by 2% from the current rate of 9% to 11%.

argAgainst.text: The argument against says the tax increase would not be needed if the City Council funded streets, police and fire services in the regular annual budget.
argAgainst.excerpt: Measure B’s tax increase wouldn’t be needed, if only councilmembers would safeguard our streets, police, and fire services in the regular, annual budget.
argAgainst.location: Argument against Measure B, middle of argument

plainEnglish.text: Adopts an ordinance that bars Los Altos from selling, leasing, conveying, or declaring as surplus land its ten City-owned Downtown Parking Plazas, or authorizing new uses or changes that would diminish protected trees or parking, unless separately approved by a majority of voters. Two Parking Plazas may be developed for affordable housing without a vote.
plainEnglish.excerpt: Shall the Ordinance, which prohibits the City of Los Altos from selling, leasing, conveying, or declaring as surplus land the ten City-owned Downtown Parking Plazas for any reason, or from authorizing new uses or physical alterations that would diminish protected trees or parking availability, access, or convenience, unless separately approved by a majority of voters, except that two Parking Plazas may be developed for affordable housing without a vote, be adopted?

yes.text: A yes vote prohibits the City from selling, leasing, conveying, declaring surplus, or permanently repurposing the Downtown Parking Plazas for any use other than surface parking without a majority vote of the City’s voters.
